findings.note: "this is often the question that makes people freeze. Many owners think the clutter has to be explained away..." is an unsupported frequency and belief claim about owners. It states no law, figure or fact about the transaction, so it is a wording preference only. Plainer wording such as "this can be the question that makes people freeze. You may wonder whether..." would remove it.

claim_checks.note: Text says the disclosures the rules require are made on a copy of the Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement form. Matches Civil Code 1102.6(a) as in the ledger; no form contents described.
Text says the rules apply, with an exception, to a transfer by sale of single-family residential property. Keeps the exception; does not flatten it.
Text says any waiver of the requirements is void as against public policy. The plain-words restatement (cannot make the requirement go away by agreement) stays within the waiver rule.

cards.issue: Unsupported frequency wording: "often the question that makes people freeze. Many owners think..."
cards.evidence: No ledger claim supports a frequency about owners; editorial standards section 5 / V1 calibration rule 3
cards.fix: Use "can be the question that makes people freeze. You may wonder whether the clutter has to be explained away."
